title: Migrate operational records with explicit preservation and disposition
statement: The system shall migrate only explicitly supported operational source records into a selected replacement store with attributable source identities and a complete disposition of the selected scope, preserving meaning and required originals and preventing activation or retirement while unresolved dependencies would be lost.

what.problem: A storage conversion can lose unsupported records, unresolved findings or exact evidence, or misrepresent old approvals as current.
what.desired_outcome: Maintainers can account for every selected source and rely on one coherent operational destination without losing historical meaning.

why.rationale: The refined IR-003 need requires this independently assessable outcome while preserving historical meaning and current work.

stakeholders: Engineering agents acting for the user

conditions: When adopting a replacement operational storage representation.

contexts: Selected project operational records, retained evidence and explicitly selected local source or destination scope.

how.approach: Use explicit scope and state identities, preserve original meaning and unrelated work, and report complete, unavailable, conflicting or failed outcomes according to the criteria below. Physical storage, commands and allocation remain downstream decisions.

how_much.scope: One selected project and declared finite operational scope; no hosted storage, automatic history merging, recovery of destroyed copies, or numerical performance/recovery guarantee. Current-model understanding remains owned by SR-004/005.

acceptance_criteria: Before publication, migration identifies selected source content and identities and classifies each record as supported for import, retained archival evidence, or blocked pending disposition; counts alone do not establish semantic equivalence.

Imported records preserve stable identities, actor decisions, unresolved findings, relationships, original subject identities and assessment meaning; source format, original location and content identity remain attributable.
Unsupported historical formats remain archival and do not acquire runtime support or renewed approval; active work that depends on them blocks activation until a responsible disposition is recorded.
Required original bytes, uncommitted source content and required artifacts remain recoverable. Migrating records does not itself authorize source deletion; SR-024 governs retirement.

Changed source identity, interruption, conflicting destination content or an invalid final reference prevents partial activation and preserves sources and unrelated destination work. A retry cannot duplicate already imported identities or silently merge conflicts.
Activation identifies one authoritative operational destination and reconciles current readers and writers; no permanent dual-write or silent legacy fallback is established.
assumptions: Required retained source material and supported interpretation information are accessible; failure of that premise is reported explicitly.
constraints: A successful storage operation grants no engineering approval or action authority.

sources.basis: Draft derivation from the refined IRs and RR proposal; no approval, implementation or satisfaction claim.
